rerun_note: The second protocol run was used to fix a construction defect (D-1, below) discovered by inspecting run 1's output, NOT to obtain a more favourable P1-P5 result. P1, P2, P3, P4 and P5 are BIT-IDENTICAL between run 1 (results_run1_raw.json, preserved unedited) and run 2 (results.json, the delivered/authoritative file) -- verified field-by-field, reported in report.md. Only the graded family's five INTERIOR t-values (0.05, 0.10, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75), which feed no P-criterion, differ between the two runs. Both runs are preserved; results_run1_raw.json is not deleted or overwritten, per the immutable-run-record rule.

deviations.what: The graded family Q_t = QR(sqrt(1-t) E_S + sqrt(t) G), implemented literally per the handoff's text (E_S a d x beta coordinate-selector matrix with unit-norm columns; G a d x beta iid standard-Gaussian matrix, UNNORMALISED), is badly scale-mismatched: a d x beta iid standard-Gaussian matrix has typical column norm sqrt(d) (~10 at d=100), against E_S's column norm of exactly 1. So the mixing weights sqrt(1-t) and sqrt(t) do NOT produce a gentle interpolation -- by t=0.01 the term sqrt(t)*G already dominates sqrt(1-t)*E_S in magnitude for most columns, and by t=0.05 the resulting subspace's principal angle to the pure coordinate-aligned subspace is already ~89 degrees (measured: t=0.01 -> 67.7 deg, t=0.02 -> 81.2 deg, t=0.05 -> 89.1 deg, at d=100, beta=30, replicate j=0). Run 1's graded-family diagnostic accordingly shows a near-vertical cliff between t=0 and t=0.05 rather than a graded decay, and 3 of 4 cells fail strict monotonicity (small, noise-level, non-monotone wiggles among interior points that have already collapsed to near-Haar).
deviations.why_P1_through_P5_are_unaffected: P3 uses only t=0 (pure E_S, G does not enter the formula at all when sqrt(t)=0) and t=1 (pure G; the G-normalisation is a POSITIVE PER-COLUMN rescaling of G, and standard unpivoted QR is invariant under independent positive per-column rescaling of its input matrix -- proved in measure.py's build_graded_Q docstring and confirmed numerically, run-1-vs-run-2 max abs difference in Q at t=0 and t=1 is exactly 0.0). P4 uses only t=0. P5 uses only the P3 quantity (departure = mean_t0 - mean_t1). None of P1, P2 (real/unreduced/lll/haar arms; independent of the graded-family construction entirely), P3, P4 or P5 depends on the interior t-values, so all five are numerically identical between the pre-fix (run 1) and post-fix (run 2) results, verified field-by-field.
deviations.fix_applied_before_run_2: G's columns normalised to unit L2 norm before mixing: G <- G / ||G_col||, per column, so E_S and G sit on a comparable scale and sqrt(1-t)/sqrt(t) behave as genuine convex-combination-like weights.
deviations.consequence_for_the_monotonicity_check: In run 2 (the delivered results.json), the coordinate-alignment departure is strictly monotone non-increasing across all 7 t-grid points in ALL FOUR cells (6/6 interior steps decreasing in every cell), giving a clean directional reading per KN-TECH-1a5b7e's monotonicity refinement -- run 1 (preserved as results_run1_raw.json) achieved this in only 1 of 4 cells.
deviations.when_found: After run 1 completed, before writing report.md, by inspecting the graded_family_summary field and finding the near-flat interior sequence implausible against the sensitivity-demonstration design rationale (RT-20260806-d008e0's own exploratory numbers showed a smooth multi-step decay); confirmed by an independent principal-angle diagnostic (not part of measure.py) before touching the code.
deviations.amendment_status: This is a CODE FIX to the delivered measure.py, applied and re-run within this task's own budget (protocol run 2 of 2), not an edit to prediction_frozen.json (which declares no numeric threshold on the interior-t monotonicity in the first place -- only P1-P5, all unaffected, are declared gates). No frozen prediction number was adjusted; nothing was re-scored against an adjusted prediction.
